steps.decide: Whether one section opens at a time or several, and what the content demands
Whether the header is a heading with a button inside, so screen-reader navigation still works
Whether open state is linkable and whether the first section opens by default
How the reveal moves, and what happens to a reader who opened several
When an accordion is the wrong control

rules.statement: Single-open is for short answers to parallel questions; multi-open is for independent sections a reader may compare, and the choice is stated in the design record.
Each header is a real heading containing a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, so heading navigation still finds the sections when they are collapsed.
The open section is in the URL when the section matters enough to share; nothing opens by default above the first viewport, because a collapsed answer is what makes an accordion cheaper than prose.
The reveal animates height with a measured value inside the 60–240 ms band, and reduced-motion shows the content with no height animation and no loss of information.
An accordion never hides the answer to the question the page exists to answer, and never hides required form fields or legal text.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a section that loads its body on open keeps that body for the life of the page; a late response for a closed section is stored and never re-opens it

motion.motion: the panel expands over 180ms to its measured height
motion.reducedMotion: the panel appears at full height instantly

transitions.trigger: an open section fetches its body

motion.motion: the panel holds its opening height over 120ms and shows a static placeholder
motion.reducedMotion: the placeholder appears with no animation and the height does not change

motion.motion: the body fades in over 140ms inside the panel
motion.reducedMotion: the body appears instantly and the panel keeps its width

motion.motion: the panel shows a retry note over 120ms
the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.motion: the control returns to pending over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the control returns to pending instantly

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Answer a set of parallel short questions on one page without making the reader scroll past the ones they do not need.
useCases: skim section titles before committing to read one
nicheDifferences: An accordion is a reading aid, not a hiding place
If the page's main answer is behind a closed section, the page is slower than plain prose
inputs: the number of sections and whether they are parallel
whether the open section must be linkable
anatomy: a panel per section with aria-labelledby
a chevron that rotates as a secondary cue
an optional loading and error region per panel
styling: headers are 44 px tall with the whole row clickable
open panels get a subtle divider, not a colour flood
a11y: each header is a button inside a heading, never a div with onclick
aria-expanded and aria-controls are correct and update
the panel is not focus-trapped and is reachable by Tab in reading order
content is not hidden from assistive technology when open
responsive: at 320 px headers wrap to two lines without truncating the question
long answers keep the measure and never open into a horizontal scroller
the reveal never leaves a blank half-screen on small heights
copy: headers are the questions themselves, in the reader's words
the first sentence of an answer answers the question
no 'Click to expand' inside an already-labelled header
alternatives: plain headings and prose when every answer matters
tabs when only one section is ever read at a time
a disclosure for one optional block inside a form
acceptance: headers are headings containing buttons with correct aria-expanded
the reveal stays inside the 60–240 ms band and moves nothing else
required content and legal text are never collapsed
failureCases: sections use divs with onclick and screen readers cannot tell they expand
the reveal animation leaves the panel at half height on a slow device
the answer to the page's main question is hidden by default
the open state is lost on reload
